Please avoid flexible arrays:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/bf554b2a15505052e7f6803f8ff728465193a0b6/CONTRIBUTING.md#L301-L314

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/bf554b2a15505052e7f6803f8ff728465193a0b6/CONTRIBUTING.md#L272-L278
Acknowledged

Please avoid more packed structs:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/bf554b2a15505052e7f6803f8ff728465193a0b6/CONTRIBUTING.md#L298-L299
Acknowledged
Done
Taking longer than expected to implement this pattern. Will push it ASAP.
Understood. Thanks for the effort.
Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, I have implemented the iterator pattern now.
Can you please reference the spec, version, and section or relevant tables?
Done
Hi Aditya, thanks for adopting the iterator pattern here, I think it's helpful.
Generally, while it is part of the API/ABI, users should use the wrapper macros instead. I'd prefer we drop this from the changelog.
Done
Can you please include the code to do so in the example? Otherwise it's not clear how `iter` should be initialised.
Done
Please make sure your test cases cover all branch paths for this condition.
Done
Done
Please never reach into `buf` directly. The internals can only be accessed safely through the msgbuf APIs. You should likely use `pldm_msgbuf_span_remaining()` here.
Done
Done
Do we need the precise calculation? Can we not rather just assume the remaining buffer length and error out later?
Done
Is it expected that library users will set up `iter` in this fashion as well? Or is this an artefact of the test case?
Yes, it was expected the library user would setup the `iter`. This doesn't seem ergonomic. So, I have changed the API. Now, the iterator is initialized by the decode function

This should be `ASSERT_EQ()`. The `EXPECT_EQ(effecter_count, 2);` below cannot be sensible if `rc` is not `0`.

Please fix any similar cases throughout.
Done
If there are no names then we shouldn't enter the loop body, right? We could instead `ASSERT_TRUE(false)` here?
Done
`ASSERT_TRUE(false)`
Done

Done
Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, really sorry for the delay in response; I was caught up in some other things. I have addressed your review comments.
That's okay, there's no rush 😊
Hi Aditya - my main concern is around the user experience without providing the nested iterator to extract the name entries themselves. Details inline.
Hmm, I think this should include the common header as well. Was there a reason not to do so?
Good catch. Updated PLDM_PDR_EFFECTER_AUXILIARY_NAMES_MIN_LENGTH to 15 (terminusHandle + effecterID + effecterCount).
See comment about nested iterators below.

Addressed. Replaced the flat pldm_effecter_auxiliary_name struct (which exposed raw names_data) with a nested iterator design. The inner pldm_platform_effecter_aux_name struct now provides decoded tag, tag_length, name, and name_length directly.

Can we please prefix symbols declared in the platform header with `pldm_platform_`?

I recognise this isn't historically consistent. I've asked for it here:


https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/8f18fe3355042d41b285f493382e82628715718f/CONTRIBUTING.md#L267-L269

Please fix throughout your patch.
Done. All new symbols are now prefixed with `pldm_platform_`
My reading is we actually need nested iterators here. The outer one is to iterate effectors, and the inner one is to iterate the names.

I have made the changes. The outer iterator (foreach_pldm_platform_effecter_auxiliary_name) iterates effecters, and the inner iterator (foreach_pldm_platform_effecter_aux_name) iterates the (language tag, UTF16 name) pairs within each effecter.
This isn't decoding the names so much as the effecters. Another iterator is needed to decode the names for each effector.
Agreed. Renamed the outer decode to clearly reflect it decodes effecter entries and added a separate decode function for the individual name strings.
I think this is a bit unkind to the user, hence the suggestion for nested iterators.
Addressed with the nested iterator design. Users no longer need to manually parse raw names_data bytes. The inner iterator decodes each (language tag, UTF16 name) pair directly.
Hi @andrew@codeconstruct.com.au, I have addressed your comments.

Can you please add the `dsp:` prefix also (as this change implements things specified by a DMTF Standard Publication)?

```
dsp: platform: Add iterators for effecter auxiliary names
```
Is there a reason this can't reference v1.3.0 instead? v1.2.0 is now 7 years old, with several new revisions published in the intervening time.
I suggest removing this. The list is evident from the patch itself.

See the documentation here:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/4509e841f6a4cad2411aa00db7cefac52330f9d2/CONTRIBUTING.md#L469-L500

In my opinion your change falls into the "simple" case there - listing just the commit subject is enough.

I understand the rest of the file isn't really organised this way, but my preference is that length macros are defined immediately below their relevant struct.

Can you please move this?

If you're going to represent the `tag` member as `const char *` then I expect we can omit `tag_length` as you're stating that `tag` is a valid C string. If it's not a valid C string (which we should be wary of if it's pointing into the message buffer) you should use `struct variable_field` instead.

See comment above.

However, for the purpose of multi-byte string encodings I've come to the conclusion that we shouldn't shoot for a valid representation there. We should instead punt to the user's string decoding implementation by only presenting them with a `struct variable_field`.
I prefer you move these declarations down below with the other hunk.

Can you please use the uncontracted `auxiliary` form consistently throughout your change?

I've pushed a change to `CONTRIBUTING` to document why:
I think your commit message needs to be updated to reflect your changes in the code. I see that `*_platform_*` is missing here but the code has it.
Hopefully all those comments make sense - I didn't realise I had drafts lying around, and intended only to respond to Vishnu's comment.

I think you should move this to the top of the list

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/c5b9e923622ecb03739cc226d436f42f10ab9d09/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L49
Return value is silently dropped. I would suggest check return value in case of failure.

It's not intended that the return value be checked here. The time to check return values is when the variable the field is extracted _to_ is used _before_ the implementation returns to the caller. For example, how `pdr->effecter_count` is tested above on lines 3444-3447, as it is used below on line 3453. If it's not used then no explicit test is necessary: the failure tests are batched up by calls to the `pldm_msgbuf_complete*()` APIs. This improves ergonomics in the implementation as this way we don't require tests after every extraction (or insertion).
This API is missing from the changelog.
Same as my above comment on return value silently dropped.
Same as my previous comment on missing entry in changelog.
